learning: If slalom line loss falls to 1.0 or below with finishes at or above 2/20, keep kd 0.8 and hold geometry. If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.35, return kd to 0.6. If slalom line loss is unchanged or worse, the next controller test is base_speed 0.9, not geometry. Mass 0.6 kg is the only open geometry exploration, and it should be tested alone.
notes: Race 8 platform with wheel_track reverted to 0.12 m after race 9 lost slalom finishes. Only kd changes (0.6 to 0.8) against race 8, to test slalom response.
rationale: Race 9 (wheel_track 0.10 m, kp 2.7, kd 0.5) scored 700.30, below race 8's 742.12. Slalom finishes fell from 2/20 to 0/20 and slalom line loss rose from 1.0 to 1.25, so the narrower track did not help slalom. I therefore take the Builder's fallback and revert wheel_track to 0.12 m, which restores the exact race 8 platform: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03, y = 0.06, body 0.12 by 0.12 m, 0.8 kg, 3 cm wheels, 12 cm track. The race 8 controller was kp 3.2, kd 0.6, base_speed 0.95. Race 8 slalom reached 2/20 finishes at 2.67 s mean, with line loss at 1.0 and max_error at 0.0594, so the time margin is about 0.33 s. I change one controller variable: kd from 0.6 to 0.8. Derivative action should damp the faster response from kp 3.2 at the slalom direction reversals, where line loss occurs. I keep kp, base_speed and the weights unchanged, so the result can be read against race 8. I do not lower base_speed, because slalom already uses most of its 3 s budget. Expected result, not yet measured: slalom line loss at or below 1.0 and finishes at or above race 8's 2/20. If slalom line loss rises or oval steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35, kd 0.6 is restored.
